people.imagined: The ferry deck at midday, mid-strait. He has just told a joke to a stranger who does not know he is the head of the sect. His laugh is carrying across the water, and he is fanning himself with a folded grey sail-cloth fan.
people.subject: The moment: on a ferry deck in a bright sea wind he throws his head back in a huge laugh, a grey fan in one hand, having just told a joke to a stranger who does not know he is the head of the sect. Face (most important: the laugh and the salt in the beard): a brown, loose, rubbery face with deep laugh lines, a wide mouth open in laughter showing strong teeth, a short beard salted with white, small bright dark eyes squeezed shut with delight, a big nose peeling at the tip; about fifty. Hair: grey-black, wind-blown, gathered at the nape with a sea-green silk ribbon and a pale shell hairpin, loose strands round the face. Body: tall, loose-jointed, long arms, an easy lounging stance with one hip against the rail. Clothing: the head's richest robes worn carelessly: a dark-amber silk storm-robe hanging open over layered salt-white and sea-teal silk, the crossed collars studded with small pearls and embroidered with silver waves and tiny boats; a translucent sea-green gauze over-robe rippling like water; wide sleeves pushed back from brown forearms; a sash of knotted green silk cord with a pale shell pendant. Hands and objects: a folding fan of grey sailcloth on pale wooden ribs held open in the right hand; on the left forefinger a ring of carved bone. Power: a strong teal aura of Water qi ripples round him like a swell, with pale streaks of wind and glittering spray motes lifting off the fan. Background: a grey-green sea, the rope rigging and sail of a ferry, blurred, gulls turning in the mist. Light: silvery spray-light from the upper left with a bright rim glow along his shoulders. Expression: roaring, careless good humour.

people.imagined: On the tide hall's stone steps at dusk, with the great crab's shell on her back like a door. She stands looking at the moon coming up over the cliffs of an abbey she has not seen in years, quietly deciding not to say what she wants.
people.subject: The moment: at dusk on the stone steps of the tide hall she looks out to sea at the moon rising over the cliffs of an abbey she has not seen in years, quietly deciding not to say what she wants. Face: a thin, severe, finely lined face with high cheekbones, a long straight nose, deep-set dark eyes, a thin pale mouth that gives nothing away; about forty-five. Hair (a feature): black with broad white streaks from the temples, drawn into a severe knot at the nape and held by a long bone-white hairpin. Body: thin, upright, an austere teacher's carriage, the heavy shell hardly bending her. Clothing: an elder's robes of salt-white and sea-teal silk in three crossed collars embroidered with silver waves, a translucent sea-green gauze over-robe that stirs in the sea wind, long narrow sleeves edged with silver boats, a sash of knotted green silk cord with a pale shell pendant, the hem damp with spray. Hands and objects: on her back a huge brown crab shell as big as a door, ridged and barnacle-spotted, held by a silk strap across the chest; in her right hand a round bronze mirror turned toward the moon, its edge green. Power: a calm teal aura with a darker green thread of Wood qi at her hands, and faint ripples of light on the mirror, as strong as an elder's. Background: a darkening sea, a pale rising moon, tidal rocks, blurred in mist. Light: blue dusk from the left, moon-silver on the mirror and a soft glow along her cheek. Expression: reserved, watchful, a faint ache.

people.imagined: At nightfall on the quay, carrying the ferry's stern lamp ashore in both hands like a funeral lantern. He is not smiling; he has not missed a crossing, and the lamp is lit.
people.subject: The moment: at nightfall on a stone quay he carries the ferry's stern lamp ashore in both hands, held low and reverent like a funeral lantern; he is not smiling, he has not missed a crossing, and the lamp is lit. Face: a square, silent, weathered face with a heavy jaw, a short flat nose, small dark steady eyes under heavy brows, a closed mouth; stubble; about forty-five. Hair: black going grey, tied up in a plain knot with a dark pin under a knotted band of salt-white silk. Body: short, square, thick-set, a rooted stance, shoulders as wide as a stern post, as if the deck were never going to move. Clothing: salt-white silk robes in layered collars with sea-teal borders embroidered with small silver boats, over them a glossy dark-amber silk storm-robe of an elder's rank, long to the knee and fastened with three horn buttons, the lowest one missing; a sash of knotted green silk cord with a pale shell pendant; the clothes are kept clean and a little damp. Hands and objects: a heavy old stern lamp of bronze and horn with a steady yellow flame held in both hands, its light on his chin; a heavy iron anchor hook hangs at his belt on a tassel; tar blackens under his fingernails. Power: a faint teal glow of Water qi gathers in the dark round his boots, steadier than it looks. Background: a dark quay, a moored ferry with a dim sail, harbour lights in the mist, rope bollards and the lit window of the ferry office. Light: the lamp warm from below, cool blue spirit-light elsewhere with a thin rim along his shoulders. Expression: solemn, silent, devoted.

people.imagined: A mangrove quay in the rain. She stands in her dead husband's oilskin cut down to fit, jaw set, looking at the sea where he went, her hand tight on the rail, the word lending in her mouth.
people.subject: The moment: at a rain-wet mangrove quay she stands with her fist on a rail, jaw set, staring at the sea where her husband went, the word lending in her mouth. Face (most important: the burnt-dark face): a tall woman's long face burned very dark by sun and wind, high cheekbones, a strong nose, narrow black eyes, thick straight brows drawn down, a wide set mouth; a thin white scar on the chin; about forty-four. Hair: black, braided in two long plaits wrapped round the head and bound with sea-green silk cord and a pale shell comb. Body: tall, broad-shouldered, strong-armed, a hard upright stance. Clothing: her dead husband's dark-amber silk storm-robe cut down at the sleeves and hem to fit her, the high collar slick with rain, worn over salt-white and sea-teal silk with silver wave embroidery at the crossed collars and a translucent green gauze sleeve-wrap darkened by wet; a sash of knotted green silk cord with a pale shell pendant. Hands and objects: the right fist gripping a wet rope rail; in the left a small stone seal on a cord wrapped round the fingers. Power: pale teal Water qi condenses as drifting rain-motes round her fists, colder and tighter than the weather. Background: green mangrove roots, grey rain, a dark sea, blurred in mist. Light: soft grey rain-light from the upper left; a thin band of pale spirit-light along the horizon outlines her cheekbone and the wet shine of the amber collar. Expression: a grim, level stare held on the water, jaw tight, the look of someone who will wait out the tide.

people.imagined: The shipyard at dawn, shavings in the air. He stands over a half-built third hull and gently smooths a rib with the three-fingered left hand, saying quietly that the hulls were sound.
people.subject: The moment: at dawn in the shipyard, shavings in the air, he stands bent over the rib of a half-built third hull and gently smooths it with the three-fingered left hand, saying quietly that the hulls were sound. Face (most important: sawdust in the eyebrows): a long, kind, stooped face with grey eyebrows full of pale sawdust, deep-set pale eyes, a hooked nose, a thin grey beard, a patient mouth; about fifty-five. Hair: thin grey, gathered in a small knot with a wooden pin, a fine fall of sawdust at the temples. Body: stooped, narrow, long arms like a cane raftsman's, a slow careful stance. Clothing: robes of salt-white and sea-teal silk, kept spotless though sawdust clings to the shoulders, crossed collars embroidered with silver waves, sleeves tied back with green silk cord, a sash of knotted green silk cord with a pale shell pendant, a dark-amber silk work-vest of his craft; an elder's quiet dignity rather than show. Hands and objects: the left hand with only three fingers (thumb, forefinger, middle) lying on the dark ribs; the right holding a small wooden plane, a pale curl of agarwood falling from it. Power: a green Wood glow and a few drifting leaf-bright motes gather round the three-fingered hand where it touches the ribs. Background: the great skeleton of a ship in dark agarwood ribs, morning haze and mist, blurred. Light: low golden dawn from the upper left through floating dust, threads of gold catching the sawdust. Expression: a quiet, stubborn tenderness in the lowered eyes, unhurried, as if listening to the wood.

people.imagined: The ferry office on the quay at noon. A traveller's fare lies in a heap of white shell coin; she taps one on her teeth, counting, her eyes already on the next customer's face.
people.subject: The moment: in the ferry office at noon she taps a small white shell coin against her front teeth, counting a traveller's fare, her eyes already up on the next customer's face. Face: a lively, sharp, round face with quick hazel eyes, thin high brows, a snub nose, a wide mouth with a coin at the lips, greed and honesty at once; about forty. Hair: black with a few grey strands, in a high bun pinned with a pale shell comb and a slim jade hairpin, two grey hairs escaping at the left temple. Body: sturdy, neat, brisk, leaning forward at the counter. Clothing: salt-white silk robes with a clean sea-teal crossed collar embroidered with tiny silver boats, sea-green gauze sleeves tied back with knotted green cords, a sash of green silk cord with a pale shell pendant; graceful silk of a steward's rank. Hands and objects: the right hand holds up a pale shell coin with a hole; the left sweeps a pile of shell coins into a wooden till shaped like a tray; a large closed book with a plain cloth cover on the counter. Power: a faint pale-teal shimmer of Water qi lies on the coins, little glints that follow her fingers. Background: a bright ferry office with a window onto masts and drifting sea-mist, blurred. Light: pearly window light from the upper left, a flash of glint from the coin at her teeth. Expression: a quick bright look, honest and shrewd at once, with a hint of appetite at the corner of the mouth.

people.imagined: On the stranded whale's beach at dawn. A small girl with pale eyes stands at the waterline with a whale's tooth on a cord, looking to the open sea the way the whale came, wanting to know her first words.
people.subject: The moment: at dawn she stands in shallow surf on the stranded whale's beach, a small girl looking far out to the horizon with her lips parted, wanting to know her first words. Face (most important: the pale eyes and sea-burnt skin): a small, brown, sea-burnt face with a stubborn chin, very pale, almost colourless grey eyes wide and unblinking, a short nose, a mouth slightly open as if about to speak; about eighteen. Hair: dark, salt-stiff, cropped short and uneven, a wisp across her cheek, a single pale shell clip. Body: small, slim, strong, bare-legged, a wild balance, toes gripping the wet sand. Clothing: the simplest graceful outer-disciple robe of salt-white silk with a sea-teal crossed collar and a single line of green stitching at the cuffs, a translucent gauze sleeve wet to the knee, a green silk cord belt knotted twice at the left hip; bare feet. Hands and objects: a large pale whale's tooth on a cord at her throat, glowing like old ivory against her brown skin; a small folded grey fan in the right hand. Power: a faint pale-blue Water glow and a few wind-motes swirl round her feet and the tooth. Background: a long grey rock shaped like a whale at the tide line with a pale gull standing on it, thin surf curling at her ankles, pearly mist. Light: soft pink dawn from the upper left with a gentle rim of glow on her wet shoulders. Expression: wondering, wild, hungry for an answer.

people.imagined: At the ferry's rail, lazily coiling a rope for the six-thousandth crossing. He rubs the ring of rope burn round his wrist and looks past the far shore at the open sea, bored and amiable.
people.subject: The moment: leaning on a ferry rail he idly coils a rope for the six-thousandth crossing, rubbing the ring of rope burn on his wrist and gazing past the far shore at the open sea with a lazy amiable yawn. Face: a young, easy, handsome-ish face with a wide lazy grin, half-lidded brown eyes, tousled brows, a bit of stubble, a crooked tooth; about twenty. Hair: dark brown, sun-streaked, uncombed, tied with a bit of green silk cord. Body: long, loose, lounging, his back curved against the rail, one foot hooked behind the other ankle, the sunlit side of his neck sunburnt red. Clothing: the simplest graceful outer-disciple robe of salt-white silk worn open at the neck with a small shell button at the collar, a sea-teal border at the hem, the sleeves cut off lazily at the shoulder, a green silk cord belt; barefoot. Hands and objects: a conspicuous pale ring of scar and rope burn round the right wrist; a coil of rope in his lap and a small iron anchor charm at his hip on a tassel; a bit of green twine tied round the left finger as a reminder he never keeps. Power: none but a faint blue-green glint of Water qi on the sea behind him. Background: a taut square sail of grey silk-cloth with a lighter square panel sewn in, a gull on the yard, low far-off green hills, spray-mist. Light: bright silvery sea light from the upper left, coins of glitter on the water. Expression: lazy, sociable, a little wistful.

people.imagined: In the yard beside the third hull, adze in hand. The cut through her eyebrow shows white. She stands very still because someone has leaned on the hull, and she has decided what to do about it.
people.subject: The moment: in the yard beside the third hull she stands very still, adze lifted, eyes cold on someone out of frame who has leaned on the hull, having decided what to do about it. Face (most important: a white scar cutting through the left eyebrow): a young, narrow, hard face with a white adze scar splitting her left eyebrow in two, level dark eyes, a straight nose, a set jaw, a thin mouth; about seventeen. Hair: black, in a single short braid pinned up with a dark iron pin. Body: slim, wiry, forearms thick for a girl and scarred with small white nicks from chisels, weight on the back foot like someone ready to throw. Clothing: the simplest graceful outer-disciple robe of salt-white silk with a deep sea-teal crossed collar, a dark-amber silk work-vest, sleeves tied back with green silk cord, a sash of knotted green cord; kept hard and neat, a few tool-pockets stitched across the chest holding a wooden spike, a nail and a stub of charcoal. Hands and objects: a short wooden adze with a curved iron blade raised in the right hand; the left rests flat on a dark hull plank; blackened tar on the fingers. Power: a thin teal glint of Water qi runs along the blade's edge, cold and quiet. Background: the dark curved ribs of a boat on the slips and a stack of long agarwood planks with their ends painted white, a half-open yard door, mist. Light: cold grey-blue spirit-light from the upper left, fine pale sawdust hanging in it and catching on her sleeves. Expression: cold, silent, terrible patience.

people.imagined: The deck, evening. He counts the passengers with his lips moving and is wrong again, quietly trying a second time, a folded passenger list half out of his sleeve.
people.subject: The moment: on the ferry deck in the evening he counts passengers off-frame with his lips moving, is wrong again, and quietly tries a second time, a folded passenger list half out of his sleeve. Face: a young, round, anxious face with wide-set brown eyes, thick worried brows, a small mouth that mouths numbers, a few pimples; about nineteen. Hair: dark brown, neat, parted, tied in a short knot with a plain pale shell pin. Body: slight, a little stooped, narrow shoulders, elbows tight to his ribs, shifting from foot to foot like someone afraid of being in the way. Clothing: the simplest graceful outer-disciple robe of salt-white silk with a high sea-teal collar, a size too big at the shoulders with the wide sleeves folded back twice, a grey silk sash in a careful double bow that has begun to slip. Hands and objects: the right hand counting on the fingers against the left palm; a folded paper of notes with a thumbprint smudge sticking out of the sleeve; a small ferry token on a cord. Power: only a faint green Wood glimmer, a couple of motes near his sleeve. Background: a loose queue of passengers with baskets and a crate of live chickens, blurred; salt-white ropes rising into a grey sail and drifting mist. Light: flat pearly evening spirit-light from the upper left, washing his pale face, with a soft glow at the rim of his collar. Expression: anxious, humble, doubting.

people.imagined: Standing on a cane raft in the shoal, a long pole in her hands, singing an old island tongue without knowing the words, bare green-stained feet on wet cane, someone listening behind her.
people.subject: The moment: standing on a bobbing cane raft she poles through the shoals, mouth open, singing an old island tongue without knowing the words, with someone listening behind her. Face: a cheerful, round, sun-brown face with a gap-toothed grin, wide dark eyes, arched brows, a button nose; about sixteen. Hair: black, in two bunches tied with bits of reed and sea-green ribbon. Body: slim, strong, easy balance, knees bent to ride the sway of the raft, the pole held low and loose like a dancer's. Clothing: the simplest graceful outer-disciple robe of salt-white silk, short and sleeveless over a sea-teal under-robe, a cord belt dyed pale green, a thin string of tiny snail shells at her neck that click when she sings; bare feet stained green by raft moss on pale cane. Hands and objects: both hands on a long bamboo pole; a small bone fish-hook charm at the neck. Power: a few teal Water motes drift up from the shallows as she sings, as if answering. Background: shallow green water, a raft of pale bundled canes tied with red twine, a half-sunken reed fish trap, a heron on one leg, a far harbour wall in mist. Light: bright silvery sea light from the upper left, a gold shimmer thrown up under her chin. Expression: carefree, singing, innocent.

people.imagined: The winter of 519, on Tình Sa beach. A salt trader shipwrecked with eleven strangers is standing in driftwood and wet sand, teaching by gesture, having just found someone she can share fire with.
people.subject: The moment: memorial portrait, faded and yellowed like an old silk painting, edges darkened. On a winter beach among wreckage in the winter of 519 a shipwrecked salt trader holds her hands out to a shared fire, smiling at someone she has just found to share it with. Face: a broad, sun-darkened, generous face with strong cheekbones, bright dark eyes, thick brows, a wide laughing mouth with gaps in the teeth, a few grey hairs; about forty-five. Hair: black going grey, tied in a thick knot in a salt-stained sea-blue silk cloth, a few salt-whitened strands whipping across her forehead. Body: sturdy, broad, solid, a trader's frame. Clothing: the robes of the sect's founder as the sect remembers her: layered salt-white and sea-teal silk with a salt-stained hem, a thick cream brocade over-robe with silver waves and small boats, a translucent sea-green gauze draped over the shoulders, a sash of knotted green silk cord with a pale shell pendant. Hands and objects: both hands held to the fire, palms open and wide; at her feet a split sack of white salt and a piece of driftwood; one small shell on a cord. Power: a faint blue Water glow in the foam at her feet and a few white salt motes lifting in the firelight. Background: dark driftwood, a wrecked hull, a grey winter sea, blurred. Light: orange firelight from the lower left with pale spirit-light on the foam, the whole picture aged and softened. Expression: open, generous, warm.

people.imagined: The ferry's first quiet crossing at the age he named the saying. A calm old head sits in the stern, a runaway girl beside him, telling a ship's boy that meeting needs no history.
people.subject: The moment: memorial portrait, faded and yellowed like an old silk painting, edges darkened. At the ferry's first quiet crossing, at the age he named the saying, a calm old head sits at the stern with a hand on the oar, looking gently at a runaway girl beside him, telling a ship's boy that meeting needs no history. Face: a long, lined, kind face with a high forehead, grey-black eyes, soft white brows, a straight nose, a generous mouth in a tiny smile, a thin white beard; about fifty-five. Hair: white and thin, in a small knot with a pale jade pin. Body: tall, thin, upright, an unhurried ease, the long neck lightly bowed, bare feet crossed on the boards. Clothing: the head's robes: layers of faded white and sea-teal silk with wide sleeves that could hide both hands, silver wave embroidery at the crossed collars, a pale cloak of sea-green gauze across the shoulders, the hem lightly wet; a sash of knotted green silk cord with a pale shell pendant. Hands and objects: one hand on a long wooden oar, the other open palm-up on his knee; at the stern a small bronze lamp; on his right wrist a loop of braided dried duckweed, bright green against the faded cloth. Power: a calm pale-blue aura of Water qi like still water round him, a few pearl motes rising. Background: a calm sea, a pale horizon, a mist-blurred line of low cliffs, a few white birds, the pale curve of a sail. Light: soft pearly spirit-light from the upper left, the whole picture aged and softened. Expression: a gentle, tranquil half-smile in the soft eyes, as if nothing needed to be forgiven or hurried.

people.imagined: 1187, on the deck of the second boat, the morning he sails west past the charts, young and sure. He stands at the helm, hair blowing, looking at the horizon where a lost fleet might be, trusting.
people.subject: The moment: memorial portrait, faded and yellowed like an old silk painting, edges darkened. In 1187 on the deck of the second boat, the morning he sails west past the charts, young and sure, a captain stands at the helm in strong wind, chin high, looking at the horizon where a lost fleet might be, trusting. Face: a strong, open, sunburnt face with a square jaw, bright brown eyes full of hope, thick dark brows, a broad nose, a confident smile, a short black beard; about forty-five. Hair: black, tied back in a tail with a sea-green ribbon and whipped by wind. Body: tall, broad, upright, a born captain, stance wide with one knee bent against the roll of the deck. Clothing: a captain's richest dress: a long dark-amber silk storm-robe lifting behind him like a flag, open over salt-white and sea-teal silk, the crossed collar studded with pearls and embroidered with silver waves; a translucent green gauze sash trailing, a sash of knotted green silk cord with a pale shell pendant; a small brass pin shaped like a ship's wheel on the lapel. Hands and objects: both hands on a spoked wooden wheel, knuckles white; a brass spyglass tucked in his belt; a plain bone ring on the left hand. Power: a bright teal Water aura streams back from him in the wind and pale spray motes glitter in it. Background: a grey-blue sea, white caps, a taut sail, mist; far behind, a second ship with a pale mended sail and a single cloud on the horizon. Light: bright windy spirit-light from the upper left, the whole picture aged and softened. Expression: confident, trusting, eager.

people.imagined: The quay of Lãng Thạch at dusk. She holds the little whistle at her chest between two fingers, never blowing it since the fever, looking at the boats and thinking of the captain she was not aboard with.
people.subject: The moment: at dusk on the quay of Lãng Thạch she holds a little whistle at her chest between two fingers, never blown since the fever, looking at the boats and thinking of the captain she was not aboard with. Face: a hard, handsome, weathered face with a strong jaw, narrow dark eyes shadowed by grief, thick brows, a full mouth held shut; a patch of pale skin on the cheek from an old fever; about forty. Hair: black, in a tight sailor's braid wrapped round her head and pinned with a pale shell comb. Body: broad-shouldered, hard, a mate's confident stance, chin lifted, feet set wide, the stiff posture of someone who has stood watches for twenty years. Clothing: salt-white silk robes with a high sea-teal collar edged in blue tape, a short sea-blue silk vest with three small bone buttons, one replaced with brass, translucent green gauze sleeves rolled to the elbow, a sash of knotted green silk cord with a pale shell pendant. Hands and objects: a small bone whistle on a bleached white cord held in the right fingers, clearly visible; the left hand on a coil of rope on the quay. Power: a faint teal Water aura, a few sorrowing motes drifting off the whistle. Background: a stone quay, two coast-trader hulls at anchor with sails furled, a lantern being lit on the nearer deck, dusk mist. Light: low blue dusk from the left with a warm lantern edge, a soft rim along her braid. Expression: stubborn, grieving, shut.

people.imagined: The Strangers' Hall's long table at dusk. He ladles soup into a stranger's bowl, the old reed cuts white across both forearms, and he is smiling because someone came in out of the cold.
people.subject: The moment: at the Strangers' Hall's long table at dusk he ladles soup into a bowl held out by a stranger, smiling because someone came in out of the cold. Face: a broad, open, tired, kind face with wide-set warm brown eyes, soft brows, a large nose, a gentle wide mouth, stubble; about forty. Hair: black, thick, tied at the nape with a sea-green silk ribbon. Body: big, soft-shouldered, comfortable, bending slightly at the waist toward the bowl, the posture of someone who has fed many people. Clothing: salt-white silk robes with a sea-teal crossed collar and silver wave borders, wide sleeves rolled to the elbow, a clean pale silk apron-sash mended with two squares of different blue silk as pockets, a sash of knotted green cord, an old brown shell coin at the neck on a cord. Hands and objects: a long ladle in the right hand over a black iron pot of steaming soup; both forearms covered with thin white healed cuts like marks of reeds, plainly visible; an earthen bowl held out. Power: a faint teal Water and green Wood glow in the rising steam, mild and warm. Background: the long table with a dozen wooden bowls, a loaf of bread, a jug of water and a few weary strangers with bowed heads, blurred. Light: warm hearth light from the lower left with a soft glow, steam crossing the beam and lighting the stubble on his jaw. Expression: a warm, tired smile that says come in and sit down, his eyes soft on the stranger's face.

people.imagined: The night crossing, rowing beside the lazy boy. Wind-chapped lips sealed with wax, she looks at him without sympathy and says the ferry goes everywhere twice a day.
people.subject: The moment: seated at an oar on the ferry on a night crossing, she looks sideways at a lazy boy out of frame without sympathy, deadpan, saying the ferry goes everywhere twice a day. Face (most important: lips sealed with a shine of wax): a plain, broad, wind-chapped face with wide-set grey eyes, thick straight brows, a short nose, lips shiny with beeswax and cracked at the edges; about nineteen. Hair: dark brown, in a thick single braid wrapped round the head and tied with a green silk cord. Body: stocky, strong, upright at the oar, shoulders rolling with each stroke, feet braced against a thwart. Clothing: salt-white silk robes with a sea-teal hooded collar, a short dark-amber silk cape with its hood thrown back, a green silk cord belt tied in a flat knot, a strip of grey silk wrapped round the left wrist above the calluses; neat and graceful. Hands and objects: both hands on a long wooden oar, knuckles red from cold; a small beeswax block at her pocket edge. Power: the wake behind the oar glows pale teal, and a few Water motes follow the blade. Background: a dark sea, a stern lantern, a distant light, far shore a low dark line with two pin-points of light, a grey sail overhead, night mist. Light: a stern lamp from the upper right, warm on one cheek, blue spirit-light elsewhere, a little rain glittering in the beam. Expression: a flat dry sideways look, the corner of the mouth just easy, at peace with the long night.

people.imagined: On the shoal yard, planing a long plank for a hull he does not know the purpose of. Pale curls fall into his hair, and he works without asking.
people.subject: The moment: in the shoal yard he bends over a workbench, drawing a plane along a long plank for a hull he does not know the purpose of, pale curls falling into his hair, working without asking. Face: a young, mild, pale face with round dark eyes, soft eyebrows, a small nose, a gentle close mouth; about eighteen. Hair: black, thick, full of pale plane curls like a wreath. Body: slender, a little stooped, neat, knees slightly bent and elbows tucked, long arms pushing the plane with an even rhythm. Clothing: the simplest graceful outer-disciple robe of salt-white silk with a pale seam at the right shoulder and a sea-teal collar, sleeves tied back with green silk cord, a dark-amber silk work-sash with a pocket full of pencils and chalk; bare feet. Hands and objects: both hands on a wooden plane shaving a long pale plank, a thin curl rising; a pencil behind the ear; a small mallet at the bench; a string of fine shavings curling over his wrist. Power: a faint green Wood glimmer where the plane bites, a couple of motes. Background: a long wall of pale new planks leaning together, a barrel of tar, a half-built hull showing dark ribs against a grey sky, mist. Light: soft pearly light from the upper left, dust motes floating in it with a gentle glow at his shoulder. Expression: a mild, absorbed face turned down to his work, steady and not asking why.

people.imagined: At the till on the coast trader's boat, counting a string of shell buttons around her neck when angry. She has just been told that the whale-child wants the third boat.
people.subject: The moment: at the till on the coast trader's boat she counts the shell buttons of her necklace between finger and thumb, jaw tight, having just been told the whale-child wants the third boat. Face: a young, honest, sharply pretty face with arched dark brows pulled together, flashing black eyes, a straight small nose, a firm mouth turned down; about twenty-two. Hair: black, in a high ponytail tied with a white shell cord and a silver hairpin. Body: slender, upright, taut, spine rigid, shoulders raised a little, a clenched stillness in the neck. Clothing: crisp salt-white silk robes with a blue crossed collar stitched with a row of tiny white wave-stitches, translucent sea-green gauze sleeves tied above the elbow with green cord, a sash of knotted green silk cord with a pale shell pendant. Hands and objects: a necklace of tiny white shell buttons round her neck, the right hand counting them; a small flat wooden till with compartments of white shell coins sorted by size beside her. Power: a taut thread of teal Water qi hums in the air round her hand, tighter than her face. Background: a boat cabin with shelves, a coil of rope, a brass lantern swinging gently, a small hanging lamp, in mist. Light: lamp light from the upper left, the swinging lantern moving a slow pool of gold light over her face, a soft rim on her hair. Expression: stiff anger, held back.

people.imagined: A copy desk in the Strangers' Hall. She chews the end of the pen, ink on her lip, deciding whether a stranger's home deserves a better line.
people.subject: The moment: at a low copy desk in the Strangers' Hall she chews the end of her brush pen, ink on her lip, eyes on a small coin beside the page, deciding whether a stranger's home deserves a better line. Face (most important: ink on the lip): a plain, clever, narrow face with a long nose, hooded brown eyes, thin brows lifted slightly, an ink-black smudge on the lower lip, a sly little smile; about twenty-four. Hair: black, in two short braids pinned back with pale shell pins, a second brush stuck behind her ear. Body: slim, bent over the work, one foot tucked under her, back bowed forward like a bird over a worm. Clothing: salt-white silk robes with a sea-teal crossed collar and ink-stained cuffs, a stain of ink down the front like a dark river, wide sleeves tied back, a pale grey silk over-apron with a pocket of spare pens, a green silk cord belt. Hands and objects: a brush pen held at the mouth, the right fingertips black; on the desk a thick plain book with blank-looking pages, a small copper coin by its edge, an ink stone. Power: a faint green Wood shimmer in the wet ink, a mote or two. Background: a wooden hall with a long wall of pigeonholes stuffed with rolled paper, a window with the sea a thin bright strip, soft mist. Light: soft window spirit-light from the upper left in a long white bar across the paper. Expression: sly, patient, tempted.

people.imagined: On the freight raft at noon, resting on the pole. He listens to his sister singing, knowing the words mean something because their grandmother wept at them, and calmly poles on.
people.subject: The moment: at noon on the loaded freight raft he rests on his pole, listening with a calm half smile to his sister singing, knowing the words mean something because their grandmother wept at them, and calmly poles on. Face: a calm, wide, brown face with a broad forehead, gentle dark eyes, thick low brows, a wide quiet mouth; about twenty. Hair: black, short, bound with a strip of reed and a sea-green ribbon. Body: tall, strong, loose, a patient stance, feet apart on the cane bundles, long arms holding the pole across his thighs. Clothing: the simplest graceful outer-disciple robe of salt-white silk worn open at the throat with a faded blue stripe at the hem, a scrap of red silk tied round the upper left arm, a green silk cord belt; bare feet. Hands and objects: both hands wrapped round a bamboo pole with a visible ridge of hard callus across each palm; rice sacks tied with green cord and a small basket of live crabs on the raft. Power: a faint teal Water shimmer where the pole meets the bay, nothing more. Background: a calm shallow bay with cane rafts, a second raft poled by a small figure, a dark line of reeds, a far headland in mist, a pale sky with two thin clouds. Light: bright silvery noon light from the upper left, the water glittering round the raft in a dazzle that outlines his shoulders. Expression: an easy, quiet half smile, eyes soft toward the singing, steady as the pole in his hands.
